own_prs.title: Interpolate quantiles inside the first histogram bin
own_prs.body:
## Summary

`RunningQuantileStats` returns the first bin's lower edge for every quantile that lands in that bin. With a single bin this collapses all quantiles, including the median and maximum, to the minimum. Coarser histograms and features with substantial mass in the first bin also receive systematically lower estimates.

Use zero as the cumulative count before the first bin and apply the same within-bin interpolation used for all later bins. The zero-quantile endpoint remains at the lower edge.

## Validation

- Added six public-API regressions covering one, two, and eight bins, each with single-batch and accumulated-batch input.
- The fixture has equal populations per bin, giving a linear inverse histogram CDF with independently known quantiles. It also checks both feature dimensions and the 0%/100% endpoints.
- Original implementation: **6 failed, 45 passed**.
- `pytest tests/datasets/test_compute_stats.py -q` after the fix: **51 passed** on CPU.
- Ruff lint, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check` passed.

[The follow-up](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/commit/0edca1bc1b669d2d0a830a9b423bfcbe5372a2f0) adds @JonnyFaeth’s two skewed-population cases. Six of eight samples occupy the first bin. The tests check q25, q50 and q75 before and after shifting and scaling the data. [JonnyFaeth reported](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/5251#issuecomment-6651626623) 53 passing module tests on Windows with Python 3.12, and both new cases failed when the old behavior was restored.

- [x] CI is green on `0edca1bc`, including [Fast Pytest](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/actions/runs/42234983579/job/127950154232) and [pre-commit](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/actions/runs/42234983349/job/127950152978).

own_prs.title: Preserve JSON checkpoints when serialization or writing fails
own_prs.body:
## Summary

`write_json` opens the destination in truncate mode before serializing. A serialization error or interrupted write can therefore replace a valid checkpoint or metadata file with partial JSON.

Write into a temporary directory beside the destination, close the completed file, and then publish it with a same-filesystem atomic replacement. Failed writes clean up their temporary files and leave the previous destination intact. Successful writes preserve formatting, UTF-8 output, existing permission bits, and symlink-following behavior.

## Validation

- Regressions cover serialization failure with and without an existing destination, a partial-write failure, and failure of the final `Path.replace()` with an existing or absent destination. They check exception propagation, preservation of the previous bytes, and temporary-file cleanup.
- Success controls cover parent-directory creation, Unicode formatting, POSIX permission preservation, and writing through an existing symlink. The exact mode-bit assertion is POSIX-only; symlink creation skips only for unsupported or denied creation, while unrelated filesystem errors still fail.
- **Linux / Python 3.12:** the [validation reported for the test-only follow-up `d60d64854f7c739fc0f92e115ae8665d44f5d462`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/5250#issuecomment-6655459897) passed all **15 cases** across `tests/utils/test_io_utils.py` and `tests/utils/test_write_json.py` in an isolated utility-module run. All **12 platform-behavior simulations** passed on Linux. Suppressing the replacement error made both new replacement-failure regressions fail. Ruff lint, Ruff format, and whitespace checks passed.
- **macOS arm64 / Python 3.12.13:** [C00kieMonsta's review](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/5250#pullrequestreview-5787586249) reported **15 passed** for the same two test files on current head `88ec5cbfd71329fb2c88225e5132bab1d1d9633c`. With `io_utils.py` from base `9e5ee9859480e425a97a6836bb3fee479539beb5`, the five failure-preservation regressions failed and the three success controls passed. The tests used real local files; serialization, partial-write, and replacement failures were injected.

The platform-behavior simulations above were run on Linux; they do not establish a native Windows result for the follow-up.

This protects against failed writes and incomplete publication; it does not add an fsync-based power-loss durability guarantee.

own_prs.title: fix(features): merge vector specifications loaded from JSON
own_prs.body:
## Problem

`combine_feature_dicts` recognizes a named numeric vector only when its shape is a tuple. Reading a feature specification from JSON converts that shape to a list, causing the merge to treat it as a non-vector and overwrite earlier action/state components. Mixing a JSON-loaded specification with an in-memory one can instead append names directly to the caller's input dictionary. A JSON-loaded right-hand specification also bypasses the existing dtype-mismatch check.

## Changes

Recognize both tuple and list shapes as vector specifications. Both forms now use the existing ordered, deduplicating merge and dtype check, without changing either input.

## Validation

The regression cases serialize either or both input dictionaries through JSON, verify the complete merged specification, and check that the inputs stay unchanged. The dtype mismatch test also covers both shape representations. On the base revision: **5 failed, 3 passed**.

own_prs.body:
## Problem

`IsaaclabArenaProcessorStep` flattens state components with `view(batch_size, -1)`. A normal transposed or sliced `(B, N, M)` tensor can be non-contiguous, so processing that observation raises a stride-layout error before policy inference.

Use `flatten(start_dim=1)` for state components with extra dimensions. This preserves the batch axis and the configured component order while supporting both contiguous tensors and ordinary tensor views.

own_prs.title: fix(rl): preserve truncation flags across replay dataset conversions
own_prs.body:
## Problem

Replay-buffer conversion loses the distinction between termination and truncation. Export writes `next.done` but omits `next.truncated`; import ignores a dataset's truncation column and adds every transition with `truncated=False`. Saving and loading a time-limited rollout therefore loses its episode-ending flag, and a later export can join episodes together.

## Changes

- Write the existing `next.truncated` dataset feature alongside `next.done`.
- Read the optional truncation column and pass it to `ReplayBuffer.add`.
- When `next.done` is absent, infer terminal boundaries only for frames that are not explicitly truncated. Explicit termination and truncation flags remain independent.
- Keep truncation false for older datasets without this column.

The existing next-state reconstruction behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

Added small on-disk numeric-dataset tests covering distinct terminal/truncated flags, both flags together, and datasets with either optional column absent. The new tests fail on the base revision: **3 failed, 2 passed**.

`HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 pytest -q tests/utils/test_replay_buffer_dataset_flags.py tests/utils/test_replay_buffer.py`

Result on CPU: **24 passed**. Ruff checks, Ruff formatting, and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.

own_prs.title: fix(rl): route mixer batches only to selected sources
own_prs.body:
## Summary / Motivation

`OnlineOfflineMixer.sample()` uses the requested batch size when no offline buffer exists, but `get_iterator()` applies `online_ratio` first. An online-only iterator configured with ratio 0.25 therefore returns 2 samples when 8 were requested. The mixer also samples both sources even when one source should contribute zero samples, so a valid all-online or all-offline configuration fails if the unused buffer is empty.

## What changed

- Delegate the full requested batch size to the online iterator when there is no offline source.
- Honor `online_ratio=0` as all-offline sampling.
- Skip unused sources for zero/full ratios and one-sample batches.
- Retain the existing minimum of one online sample for positive mixed ratios.

## Validation

- Regression suite against unmodified main: 9 failed, 6 passed.
- `pytest -q tests/rl/test_data_mixer.py tests/rl/test_trainer.py tests/rl/test_sac_algorithm.py`: 55 passed on CPU with PyTorch 2.11.0 and NumPy 2.2.6.
- Ruff lint and formatting checks passed for the changed files; `git diff --check` passed.

Tests use real replay buffers, cover both sample and iterator access, and exercise synchronous and asynchronous online-only iteration. The complete repository test suite was not run.

own_prs.title: fix(rollout): enforce ring-buffer frame and memory limits
own_prs.body:
## Summary / Motivation

The rollout ring buffer removes old frames automatically at its frame limit but does not subtract their sizes from its byte counter. The reported budget therefore accumulates bytes that are no longer retained. A single frame larger than the whole memory budget also evicts existing history and is still accepted, exceeding the configured cap.

## What changed

- Evict explicitly for both the frame and byte limits so the byte count tracks the retained frames.
- Keep zero-frame windows empty with a zero byte count.
- Skip a frame that cannot fit the memory budget, preserving the previous valid history.

## Validation

- New regression tests against unmodified main: 4 failed, 1 passed.
- `pytest -q tests/test_rollout_ring_buffer.py tests/test_rollout.py`: 93 passed, 1 skipped on CPU with PyTorch 2.11.0 and NumPy 2.2.6.
- Ruff lint and formatting checks passed for the changed files; `git diff --check` passed.

The tests cover repeated time-window eviction, memory eviction, oversized frames, empty-capacity windows, draining, and existing rollout behavior. The complete repository test suite was not run.

own_prs.body:
## Summary / Motivation

VLA-JEPA rotates adjacent query/key coordinate pairs, but repeats the frequency vector as two complete blocks. The two coordinates of a pair therefore use different angles, breaking RoPE's norm and relative-position inner-product invariants. For example, rotating `[1, 2, 3, 4]` at position 1 changes its norm from 5.4772 to 4.9628.

Repeat each frequency twice and retain the position axis. This also fixes broadcasting for a single frequency. The change is confined to the training-only world predictor.

## Related issues and source

This applies the known pairwise correction proposed by echosprint in [V-JEPA 2 #15](https://github.com/facebookresearch/vjepa2/pull/15). [V-JEPA 2 #75](https://github.com/facebookresearch/vjepa2/pull/75) documented the issue while retaining the original expansion for released-checkpoint compatibility. The source and compatibility rationale are linked in the production helper and documentation.

This is separate from #4116 (multi-horizon world-model training) and #4814 (action-noise handling).

## What changed

- Match the sine/cosine layout to the existing adjacent-pair rotation.
- Document the source of the correction and training compatibility. Parameter names and shapes are unchanged, but existing world-model checkpoints produce different predictor outputs and training losses with corrected positions. Pretrained quality has not been evaluated.
- Keep the four existing world-model tests unchanged. The earlier additional 107-line test block was removed from the PR; the current diff contains only the production helper and documentation.

relevant_prs.title: fix(tdmpc): encode the OBS_IMAGE copy so custom camera keys work
relevant_prs.body:
## Summary / Motivation

`TDMPCPolicy.select_action` crashes with a `KeyError` whenever the camera feature is not named exactly `observation.image` (e.g. `observation.images.laptop`), and during training the random-shift image augmentation is silently skipped for such keys.

- There was a naming mismatch. One image with two different names. The camera image arrives as `observation.images.laptop`, and `select_action` copies it to `observation.image`. 
- `reset()` creates queues for `observation.state`, `action`, and `observation.image`, but none for `observation.images.laptop`. So, when `observation.images.laptop` was used there was no match in the queue. 
- Then `predict_action_chunk` did the rebuild using queues only and so after the rebuild from the batch only `observation.image` and `observation.state` exist. 
- So, the encoder was asking for the name that was dropped. A look-up for `observation.images.laptop` that was not there. 

`forward` applies a random shift augmentation to `observation.image` 
- With the camera named `observation.image`, the encoder reads the augmented image
- With any other name, it read the original, un-augmented image
- While we have same weights and data we have different input pixels and thus different loss. Augmentation was being computed for the second and then ignored. After the fix, both cases read the augmented copy and hence see identical pixels giving the same loss

The fix makes the encoder read `OBS_IMAGE`, which restores the pre-#550 behaviour and fixes both symptoms with a one-line change.

## Related issues

- Regression from #550 (commit 3c0a209f9), which changed the encoder from `obs_dict["observation.image"]` to the configured image key while the queue/planning path kept using `OBS_IMAGE`.
- Found while working on TDMPC `torch.compile` support (related: #2061).

## What changed

- `TDMPCObservationEncoder.forward` now encodes `obs_dict[OBS_IMAGE]`.
- New `tests/policies/tdmpc/test_tdmpc.py`:
  - `test_select_action_with_custom_image_key`: `select_action` works with a camera named `observation.images.laptop`.
  - `test_forward_is_independent_of_image_key`: two policies with identical weights, differing only in camera name, give the same training loss under the same seed and data.
- No breaking changes. For camera keys already named `observation.image`, behaviour is unchanged.

## How was this tested (or how to run locally)

- `pytest tests/policies/tdmpc/test_tdmpc.py -v`

## Title

fix(policies): make TDMPC's predict_action_chunk work for the async server

## Summary / Motivation

`tdmpc` is listed in `SUPPORTED_POLICIES` for async inference, but `PolicyServer._get_action_chunk` couldn't get actions from it (#4870):

1. `predict_action_chunk` built its input only from the observation queues that `select_action` fills. The server calls it directly on a freshly reset policy, so it raised `RuntimeError: stack expects a non-empty TensorList`.
2. It returned `(horizon, batch, action_dim)`, while the server (and ACT, Diffusion, ...) expect `(batch, chunk, action_dim)`, so `chunk[:, :actions_per_chunk]` sliced the batch axis.

This follows option (a) from the issue.

## Related issues

- Fixes: #4870
- Related: #3886 (same queue problem for Diffusion)

## What changed

- `TDMPCPolicy.predict_action_chunk` uses the queued observations when `select_action` has filled them, and the observation in `batch` otherwise (mapping the first image feature to `observation.image`, as `select_action` does).
- It now returns `(batch, horizon, action_dim)`. `select_action` transposes the chunk back before filling its time-major action queue, so its output is unchanged.
- No breaking change for `select_action`. Code that called `predict_action_chunk` directly and relied on the time-major layout will see batch-first output, like the other policies.

## How was this tested (or how to run locally)

- Added `test_tdmpc_predict_action_chunk_is_batch_first_without_select_action` in `tests/policies/test_policies.py`, for `use_mpc` True and False. It calls `predict_action_chunk` on a reset policy and checks the `(batch, chunk, action_dim)` shape, then checks the same after `select_action`. With `use_mpc=False` (deterministic) it also checks both paths and `select_action` give the same actions. Both cases fail on main and pass here.
- The reproducer from the issue now prints `(1, 5, 6)` for both calls and `(1, 2, 6)` from `PolicyServer._get_action_chunk(actions_per_chunk=2)`.
- `pytest tests/policies/test_policies.py tests/processor/test_tdmpc_processor.py -k tdmpc` and `pytest tests/async_inference` pass locally (Windows, CPU). `ruff format`, `ruff check` and `mypy --config-file=pyproject.toml` are clean on the changed files.

relevant_prs.title: feat(tdmpc): add torch.compile support for MPC planning
relevant_prs.body:
> **Depends on #4741** — its commit appears in this diff until that PR is merged; I'll rebase afterwards.

## Summary / Motivation

Part of #2061. Adds opt-in `torch.compile` support for TD-MPC's MPC planner via `compile_model` / `compile_mode` config options, following the pattern used by pi0, pi05 and smolvla.

Compiling the planner as it was had three problems. 
 - The old `plan` read `self._prev_mean` which is `None` after `reset()`. So, the compiler was specializing on the question "Is it None?" and had to re-compile. On T4 this meant an almost doubling of the compilation time (122 s + 89 s).
 -  `randint` and `arange`  created CPU tensors used to index GPU tensors. That meant a small CPU-to-GPU copy on every CEM iteration, and at compile time it made PyTorch skip CUDA graphs entirely.
 - The old `plan` stored its result (the mean) on `self` for the next step. In CUDA-graph modes, compiled outputs live in memory that is overwritten on the next call, so with `reduce-overhead` this crashed.

## What changed

- **Stateless planning core.** `plan` is now a thin eager wrapper that manages the warm-start state and calls a new stateless `_plan_step(z, prev_mean)`. The "no previous plan" case passes zeros, which is numerically identical to the old `None` branch. This is the part that gets compiled.
- **Device fix.** `torch.randint` in `estimate_value` and `torch.arange` in `_plan_step` now create their tensors on the model's device. This removes a small CPU→GPU copy per CEM iteration and unblocks CUDA graphs.
- **Config.** New `compile_model: bool = False` and `compile_mode: str = "max-autotune"` in `TDMPCConfig` (documented in the docstring). Only the planning step is compiled; training (`forward`) is unchanged.
- **Clones in `plan`.** The stored mean and returned actions are cloned, because CUDA-graph modes reuse their output memory on the next call.
- Unlike pi0, this does not call `torch.set_float32_matmul_precision`, to avoid a global numerics side effect.

## How was this tested

- **Bit-identical eager behaviour on CPU:** a seeded end-to-end run (forward + 6 `select_action` calls) gives exactly the same loss, actions and warm-start state as before the change (`torch.equal`).
- **New test** `test_compiled_plan_has_no_graph_breaks_or_recompiles` (tiny config, ~17 s on CPU cold): builds TD-MPC with `compile_model=True`, plans three times through `select_action`, and asserts no graph breaks, no guard failures, and exactly one compiled graph. Verified that it **fails** when the stateful `plan` is compiled instead (guard failure `_prev_mean is None`).
- Existing TD-MPC tests pass: 12 passed, 5 skipped (CUDA-only).
- **Benchmark** (Colab T4, torch 2.11.0+cu128, batch 2, default config, `policy.plan(z)`, `torch.utils.benchmark.Timer.blocked_autorange(min_run_time=5)`):

| Variant | First call | Median | IQR |
|---|---|---|---|
| eager | 0.37 s | 70.4 ms | 17.7 ms |
| `default` | 108 s | 55.8 ms | 0.7 ms |
| `reduce-overhead` | 86 s | 55.6 ms | 0.5 ms |
| `max-autotune` | 166 s | 56.4 ms | 0.5 ms |

The variants ran in this order in one process; later ones reuse some cached kernels, so first-call times are indicative.

  Compiled planning is ~1.2 - 1.25× faster than eager. The device fix alone made no measurable eager difference (A/B/A/B runs within noise). The CUDA-graph modes (`reduce-overhead`, `max-autotune`) are no faster than `default`. CUDA graphs remove kernel-launch overhead, but on the T4, after compilation, TD-MPC planning is dominated by real computation rather than launch overhead, so there is little left to remove. I didn't test faster GPUs, where it could make a bigger difference.

<details><summary>Benchmark script</summary>

```python

import sys
import time
import torch
from torch.utils.benchmark import Timer
from lerobot.policies.factory import make_policy_config
from lerobot.configs.types import FeatureType, PolicyFeature
from lerobot.utils.constants import ACTION, OBS_STATE, OBS_IMAGE
from lerobot.policies.tdmpc.modeling_tdmpc import TDMPCPolicy

def make_policy(compile_mode=None):
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    
    config_args = {"device": "cuda"}
    if compile_mode is not None:
        config_args["compile_model"] = True
        config_args["compile_mode"] = compile_mode
        
    cfg = make_policy_config("tdmpc", **config_args)
    
    cfg.input_features = {
        f"{OBS_IMAGE}": PolicyFeature(type=FeatureType.VISUAL, shape=(3, 84, 84)),
        OBS_STATE: PolicyFeature(type=FeatureType.STATE, shape=(6,)),
    }
    cfg.output_features = {
        ACTION: PolicyFeature(type=FeatureType.ACTION, shape=(6,)),
    }
    
    policy = TDMPCPolicy(cfg).to("cuda").eval()
    policy.reset()
    return policy

eager_policy = make_policy(compile_mode=None)
batch = {
    f"{OBS_IMAGE}": torch.rand(2, 3, 84, 84, device="cuda"),
    OBS_STATE: torch.rand(2, 6, device="cuda"),
}
with torch.no_grad():
    z = eager_policy.model.encode(batch)

for variant_name in sys.argv[1:]:
    mode = None if variant_name == "eager" else variant_name
    
    torch._dynamo.reset()
    policy = make_policy(mode)
    
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    start_time = time.perf_counter()
    policy.plan(z)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    first_call_seconds = time.perf_counter() - start_time
    
    m = Timer(
        stmt="policy.plan(z)", 
        globals={"policy": policy, "z": z}
    ).blocked_autorange(min_run_time=5)
    
    median_ms = m.median * 1000
    iqr_ms = m.iqr * 1000
    print(f"{variant_name}: first_call={first_call_seconds:.4f}s, median={median_ms:.2f}ms, iqr={iqr_ms:.2f}ms")

```
</details>

## Notes / open questions for reviewers

- **Default `compile_mode`:** I kept `"max-autotune"` for consistency with pi0/pi05/smolvla. On a T4 it gives no benefit over `"default"` and compiles ~55% slower. Happy to change the default if you prefer. I could only test on a T4, so larger GPUs may behave differently.
- **GPU random stream:** because `randint` now runs on the GPU, CUDA runs draw from the CUDA generator instead of the CPU one, so seeded GPU results are statistically equivalent but not bit-identical to before. CPU results are unchanged.
- In torch 2.11, `torch._dynamo.utils.counters["recompiles"]` is never populated, so the new test checks `guard_failures` and `unique_graphs` instead. (The pi0 test helper also asserts on `counters["recompiles"]`; it's harmless there because it checks `guard_failures` too.)
- Out of scope: compiling `forward` (training), which still has `.item()` graph breaks.

## Checklist (required before merge)

- [x] Linting/formatting run (`pre-commit run -a`)
- [ ] All tests pass locally (`pytest`)
- [ ] Documentation updated
- [ ] CI is green
- [x] Community Review: I have reviewed another contributor's open PR and linked it here: #4748

## AI assistance

I used Claude (Anthropic) as a guide. It suggested the investigation steps and the overall design (stateless core, output clones, config options), helped me interpret compiler logs, and drafted this description. I made the code changes, wrote the tests and the benchmark script, ran all the experiments, verified the results and reviewed and edited this description.

fix(vqbet): support direct single-frame chunk inference

relevant_prs.title: fix(processor): keep declared feature names through normalization migration
relevant_prs.body:
## Summary / Motivation

Migrating an ACT, TDMPC or gaussian_actor checkpoint silently leaves `observation.environment_state` unnormalized. Nothing raises. The policy runs on unnormalized input and the only symptom is that it behaves worse than it should.

What happens on a plain single-dataset checkpoint, no multi-dataset prefix involved:

| step | value |
| --- | --- |
| the policy declares | `observation.environment_state` |
| migration writes the stats under | `observation.environment.state` |
| the normalizer looks up | `observation.environment_state` |
| result | no match, feature goes through unnormalized, no error |

The reproduction from #4451, before and after this change:

```
no declared names : ['observation.environment.state']
config declares it: ['observation.environment_state']
```

The cause is in `extract_normalization_stats`, which rebuilt a feature name from a checkpoint buffer key with an unconditional `replace("_", ".")`. Any feature whose own name contains an underscore is mangled, and `OBS_ENV_STATE` is the one that ships.

The flattening is not reversible from the string alone: `observation.environment_state` and `observation.environment.state` both flatten to `observation_environment_state`. The only source of truth is the set of names the policy declares, so the caller now passes them in and they win.

## Related issues

- Fixes: #4451

## What changed

- `extract_normalization_stats` takes an optional `feature_names`. A stored name that matches a declared name is used as-is; otherwise a declared name whose dots flatten to the stored form wins; otherwise the previous reading (every underscore becomes a dot) applies.
- `main()` passes the names the config declares. `get_declared_feature_names` collects them from `input_features` / `output_features` and from the legacy `input_shapes` / `output_shapes` / `features` fields, so a checkpoint whose config still uses `input_shapes` (the case @algattik raised in review) is covered too.
- No behaviour change for a checkpoint whose config has none of those fields: with no declared names, extraction reads exactly as before. Such checkpoints have no config-level source of truth, and inventing a different heuristic would only move which names it gets wrong, which is the same gap `detect_features_and_norm_modes`'s stats-based fallback already has.

The third case is needed in practice: the `normalize.` / `input_normalizer.` family of prefixes stores the name with its dots intact, so `normalize.observation.environment_state.mean` arrives as `observation.environment_state` and matches no flattened key. Without the direct match it would fall through and be mangled again.

## How was this tested (or how to run locally)

Tests added in `tests/processor/test_migrate_policy_normalization.py`, 7 cases: the underscore name survives; declared names disambiguate the shared flattened form; an undeclared name keeps the historical reading; names without underscores are undisturbed; the dot-preserving prefix keeps a declared underscore; an undeclared feature still migrates rather than being dropped; a legacy `input_shapes` config declares feature names.

```
pytest -q tests/processor/test_migrate_policy_normalization.py
```

With `migrate_policy_normalization.py` reverted to the branch point, the six original cases go 5 failed, 1 passed; the one that stays green is `test_undeclared_name_keeps_the_historical_reading`, which pins the unchanged fallback. The seventh case imports `get_declared_feature_names`, so with the source reverted the module does not import at all.

`pytest -q tests/processor` gives 503 passed, 14 skipped, 2 failed. The two failures are `test_pi0_processor_inputs_match_openpi_reference` and its pi05 counterpart, which raise `OSError` fetching the gated `google/paligemma-3b-pt-224`. They fail identically with this change reverted.

## Checklist (required before merge)

- [x] Linting/formatting run: `ruff check` and `ruff format` on the touched files; I did not run the full `pre-commit run -a`
- [x] All tests pass locally: `tests/processor`, apart from the two pre-existing gated-repo failures noted above
- [ ] Documentation updated: none needed; the argument is documented on the function
- [x] CI is green: 6 checks pass; Build Main Docs was skipped
- [x] Community Review: #4285

## Reviewer notes

`extract_normalization_stats` is also touched by #4446 (@takashi-jp), which handles dataset-prefix cases and deliberately leaves this bug alone. Adjacent lines, orthogonal logic, and I am happy to rebase whichever lands second.

I previously had a third PR on this function, #4441. I closed it on 2026-09-08, so the add/add conflict on `tests/processor/test_migrate_policy_normalization.py` that it would have created is gone.

The case worth a second opinion is the fallback for old configs, described under *What changed*.

relevant_prs.title: fix(policies): support async/single-frame inference for Diffusion
relevant_prs.body:
## Summary / Motivation

Async inference crashes immediately when serving a **Diffusion** policy: the policy server loads the model, receives observation #0, then errors on the very first inference and never produces an action (the robot never moves). An ACT policy works on the identical setup, isolating the bug to the diffusion inference path.

Root cause: the async `PolicyServer` calls `DiffusionPolicy.predict_action_chunk()` directly with a single, un-warmed observation and never populates the observation-history queues that the synchronous `select_action()` path relies on. Diffusion conditions on `n_obs_steps` past frames (default 2), so the model requires a temporal observation dimension. With empty queues, the existing queue-less branch only gave images a length-1 temporal dimension and left `observation.state` 2D, so `generate_actions()` failed its `n_obs_steps == config.n_obs_steps` assertion (and previously raised `stack expects a non-empty TensorList`). ACT is unaffected because it has no temporal observation queue.

## Related issues

- Fixes: #3861

## What changed

- In `DiffusionPolicy.predict_action_chunk()`, the queue-less branch now expands a single frame (state `ndim==2`, images `ndim==4`, env_state `ndim==2`) along a new temporal dimension of length `n_obs_steps`, mirroring the warm-up that `select_action()` performs via `populate_queues`.
- Batches that already carry the temporal dimension (offline dataloader batches, the case added in #3822) are detected by `ndim` and left untouched, so that path is unchanged.
- No client/server changes are required; the fix is entirely inside the policy.

## How was this tested

- Unit test: added `test_diffusion_predict_action_chunk_warms_up_empty_queues` in `tests/policies/test_policies.py`, which calls `predict_action_chunk()` with a single-frame batch and empty queues (the async path) and asserts a valid action chunk is returned. Run with `pytest -q tests/policies -k diffusion`.
- On-hardware end-to-end validation (see Validation section below).

## Validation (real hardware, end-to-end)

Validated the full async pipeline on real hardware.

Setup:
- Server: RunPod, NVIDIA RTX A4000, CUDA, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.8, `policy_device=cuda`
- Client: Raspberry Pi 5, SO-101 follower, scene + wrist cameras (640x480), async over direct TCP
- Policy: diffusion (`--policy_type=diffusion`)

Before the fix: the server crashed at observation #0 with `Error in StreamActions: stack expects a non-empty TensorList`, then looped `Starting receiver` forever; no action chunks were ever generated.

After the fix: the server runs diffusion inference continuously and streams action chunks. Representative server log:

```
Running inference for observation #103
Preprocessing and inference took 0.9853s, action shape: torch.Size([1, 8, 6])
Observation 103 | Total time: 1019.97ms
Action chunk #103 generated | Total time: 1020.71ms
Running inference for observation #107
Preprocessing and inference took 0.9925s, action shape: torch.Size([1, 8, 6])
Action chunk #107 generated | Total time: 1025.91ms
```

## Checklist

- [x] Linting/formatting (ruff via CI `quality.yml`)
- [x] Tests pass (new regression test + CI; on-hardware validation above)

## Reviewer notes

- The same empty-queue stacking pattern also affects `vqbet` and `tdmpc` under async inference (they were not touched by #3822). This PR is intentionally scoped to Diffusion only; the others can be addressed as separate follow-ups.

relevant_prs.title: fix(config): preserve null and CLI overrides with policy.path
relevant_prs.body:
## Title

fix(config): preserve null and CLI overrides with policy.path

## Summary / Motivation

Loading a policy through `policy.path` in YAML/JSON loses two kinds of overrides. Explicit nulls are dropped, so saved nullable settings cannot be cleared. CLI policy arguments are filtered before the file's path is discovered, so adding a CLI override can instead fail while decoding `policy` without a `type` discriminator.

For example, an ACT checkpoint saved with `temporal_ensemble_coeff=0.01` and `n_action_steps=1` should allow:

```yaml
env:
  type: aloha
policy:
  path: /path/to/checkpoint
  temporal_ensemble_coeff: null
```

```bash
lerobot-eval --config_path=eval.yaml --policy.n_action_steps=4
```

The resolved policy now disables temporal ensembling and uses four queued actions. Previously this mixed input failed before loading the policy; placing both overrides in the file also failed because the saved coefficient remained enabled.

## Related issues

Related: #3597, #4601. Current main includes list serialization from #4739; this change preserves it.

## What changed

- Serialize explicit `None` as JSON `null`, preserving the existing boolean spelling. Omitting a key still retains its saved value.
- Extract file paths before filtering CLI policy arguments, so they reach the existing checkpoint override parser. Explicit CLI values and paths keep their precedence.
- Add real train/eval configuration-entry tests for YAML/JSON, save/reload checks, and CLI-path controls; update the existing null test and helper docstring.

Explicit nulls now reach the existing decoder instead of being ignored. To keep a saved value, omit its key. This does not introduce stricter type validation: draccus 0.11.6 also accepts null for some non-Optional scalar fields through direct CLI input.

## How was this tested

Current revision `55ad8c42`, synchronized with main `e595b790`: **119 passed** for `tests/test_yaml_policy_path.py tests/configs tests/processor/test_pi_tokenizer_configuration.py` on CPU. Includes empty/nonempty lists decoded together with null and boolean overrides. Full `pre-commit run --all-files` passed, including mypy.

The following broader CPU/GPU and inference results were collected on the original revision `da5a672b`; they were not rerun in full after this synchronization.

Against main `b6ec0060779550c0a157ae34feb89e0cf86012a8`, the selected regression cases report **11 failed, 4 passed**. With the fix:

```bash
LEROBOT_TEST_DEVICE=cpu pytest -q tests/test_yaml_policy_path.py tests/configs tests/processor/test_pi_tokenizer_configuration.py
```

**96 passed**, with the relevant optional dependencies installed. A separate local composition with #4601's current list-serialization change and its two added tests reports **30 passed**; that composition is not included in this diff.

Pretrained inference: strictly loaded weights from `lerobot/act_aloha_sim_transfer_cube_human` at `ba73b2766f1371cdc133ca4efb97eb090d744625`, using the official normalization migration, on an RTX 5070 Ti. A temporary config saved coefficient 0.01 and one action step. The fixed file-only and mixed inputs exactly matched the original working CLI-only path over 12 Aloha steps (actions/rewards; 3 model calls). Omitting the setting retained ensembling and identical before/after traces (12 calls). Original file-only and mixed inputs failed during configuration loading. This is a short inference regression check, not a task-success benchmark.

Full `tests` directory in four isolated CPU dependency tiers:

| Tier | Passed | Skipped | Failed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| base | 1390 | 413 | 0 |
| dataset | 2598 | 382 | 0 |
| hardware | 1423 | 412 | 0 |
| viz | 1394 | 412 | 0 |

These CPU tiers use Python 3.12 and same-version CPU torch/torchvision wheels (2.11.0+cpu / 0.26.0+cpu).

The same commit was also tested on a laboratory RTX 5090 with Python 3.12.3 and the locked CUDA dependencies (`uv sync --locked --extra all --extra lancedb-convert`, torch 2.11.0+cu128):

- Full `pytest tests`: **3482 passed, 118 skipped, 0 failed** with upstream CI conditions enabled. This includes the pretrained XVLA preprocessing, action-reference and reproducibility checks.
- All **19** cases skipped for needing multiple GPUs passed separately on four GPUs, including DDP/FSDP/HSDP training, changed-topology resume, checkpointing and device transfers. The **3** CPU-only numerical-reference cases also passed separately. The remaining 96 skips cover upstream CI opt-outs, gated/external fixtures, platform and hardware requirements.
- `make DEVICE=cuda PYTHON_PATH=<venv>/bin/python test-end-to-end`: **all nine targets passed**, covering ACT train/resume/eval and Diffusion, TDMPC and SmolVLA train/eval. Public Hub caches and hf-mirror.com were used on that host.

`pre-commit run --all-files` passed, followed by checks on the final changed files. Physical robots and upstream CI remain unverified; the four upstream workflows currently require maintainer approval.

relevant_prs.body:
## Title

feat(export): add `lerobot-export` CLI for ONNX/TensorRT edge deployment

## Summary / Motivation

Adds a `lerobot-export` CLI that exports trained LeRobot policies to ONNX (and
optionally TensorRT) for edge deployment on devices such as Jetson Orin Nano/NX.
Users running trained policies on Jetson-class devices need an optimized
inference format; ONNX + TensorRT FP16 provides significant speedup over
PyTorch on SM_87 GPUs without requiring the Python training stack at inference
time.

## Related issues

- Fixes / Closes: #3146

## What changed

- **New CLI** `lerobot-export` (entry point `lerobot.scripts.lerobot_export`)
  supporting `--format=onnx` (default) and `--format=tensorrt`.
- **New `lerobot.export` package** with:
  - `ExportSpec` dataclass + `register_export_wrapper` plugin registry with
    auto-discovery by naming convention (`policies/<type>/export_<type>.py`).
  - Reusable adapter primitives: `DictBatchAdapter` (Pattern A) and
    `IterativeDenoisingAdapter` ABC (Pattern B) in `export/adapters/`.
  - Three ONNX exporter backends: `dynamo`, `legacy`, and `auto` (tries dynamo,
    falls back to legacy).
  - `validate_onnx()` — post-export parity check (max_abs_error, cos_sim,
    `torch.allclose`). Supports `--validation-trials=N` for random-input trials.
  - `export_to_tensorrt()` via `trtexec` subprocess with engine cache and
    hardware guards (FP8/INT8 on SM_87 raises; FP16 on SM<80 warns).
  - `save_normalization_stats()` + `NormalizedWrapper` (opt-in
    `--fold-normalization` bakes stats as ONNX constants).
- **Per-policy adapters** co-located with each policy module:
  - `policies/act/export_act.py` — ACT via `DictBatchAdapter`
  - `policies/diffusion/export_diffusion.py` — UNet-only and full DDIM loop
    (`--diffusion-mode=ddim-N`)
  - `policies/vqbet/export_vqbet.py` — VQ-BeT via `DictBatchAdapter`
- Unsupported policies (SAC, TDMPC, PI0, SmoLVLA) raise `NotImplementedError`
  with a concrete extension guide instead of silently producing wrong output.
- **New optional dependency group** `export` (`onnx`, `onnxruntime`,
  `onnxscript`) in `pyproject.toml`; `_onnx_available` / `_onnxruntime_available`
  added to `import_utils.py`.

No breaking changes to existing APIs.

## How was this tested (or how to run locally)

**Unit tests** (31 passed, 1 skipped on macOS/MPS):

```bash
uv sync --locked --extra export --extra test
uv run pytest tests/test_export.py tests/policies/test_export_act.py \
    tests/policies/test_export_vqbet.py tests/policies/test_export_diffusion.py -sv
```

**End-to-end validation against real Hub checkpoints** (macOS/CPU, opset 18,
`--validation-trials=5`):

```bash
# ACT
uv run lerobot-export \
  --policy.path=lerobot/act_aloha_sim_insertion_human \
  --output_path=./outputs/verify_act --device=cpu --exporter=legacy \
  --validation_trials=5
# => worst max_abs_error=2.09e-06, min cos_sim=1.000000, allclose=True

# Diffusion UNet (batch_size=4, dynamic)
uv run lerobot-export \
  --policy.path=lerobot/diffusion_pusht \
  --output_path=./outputs/verify_diffusion --device=cpu \
  --validation_trials=5
# => worst max_abs_error=9.06e-06, min cos_sim=1.000000, allclose=True
```

TensorRT engine builds require CUDA + `trtexec`; the hardware-guard error paths
are covered by `tests/test_export.py::test_export_to_tensorrt_raises_without_cuda`.

## Checklist (required before merge)

- [x] Linting/formatting run (`pre-commit run -a`)
- [x] All tests pass locally (`pytest`)
- [x] Documentation updated
- [ ] CI is green
- [ ] Community Review: I have reviewed another contributor's open PR and linked it here: # (insert PR number/link)

## Reviewer notes

- **ACT + dynamo batch>1 is a known limitation**: even `--exporter=dynamo`
  produces a fixed `batch_size=1` ONNX because `ACT.forward` allocates
  `torch.zeros([batch_size, latent_dim])` inside the model, causing
  `torch.export` to specialize on the concrete value. Fixing this requires
  modifying `ACT.forward` itself and is out of scope for this PR.
- **`export/adapters/`** contains the two reusable primitives intended to keep
  future per-policy adapters thin. Feedback on the API surface is welcome.
- **TensorRT path** is tested only via error-path unit tests (no CUDA on the
  development host); a GPU CI job is a follow-up.
- Older Hub checkpoints (e.g. `lerobot/act_aloha_sim_insertion_human`) do not
  ship `policy_preprocessor.json`, so `normalization_stats.json` is written as
  `{}` with a warning — this is expected and logged clearly.

## Summary

Wave 3 (policies) of the API-docstring initiative: documents `src/lerobot/policies/` to its agreed narrow scope, following the standard in `docs/source/writing_docstrings.mdx`. `policies/` is by far the largest module in this initiative (1,636 public symbols at 36.5% coverage — roughly half the total remaining work), so rather than full coverage the scope was deliberately narrowed to `PreTrainedPolicy`/`PreTrainedConfig`/`factory.py` plus, for each of the 19 policy families, its full `Config` dataclass and the public `forward`/`select_action`/`predict_action_chunk`/`get_optim_params`/`reset` surface of the main `<Family>Policy` class. Per-policy internals (model building blocks, nested `ProcessorStep` helpers, shared backbones like `pi_gemma.py` and the new `policies/common/` utilities) remain out of scope and stay `D`-ignored.

- Documents `PreTrainedPolicy` (the abstract base every policy subclasses — `forward`, `predict_action_chunk`, `select_action`, `get_optim_params`, `reset`, `from_pretrained`, `supports_rtc`, PEFT helpers), `factory.py`'s public functions (`make_policy`, `get_policy_class`, `make_policy_config`, `make_pre_post_processors`), and `policies/utils.py`.
- For all 19 families (`act`, `diffusion`, `eo1`, `evo1`, `fastwam`, `gaussian_actor`, `groot`, `lingbot_va`, `molmoact2`, `multi_task_dit`, `pi0`, `pi05`, `pi0_fast`, `smolvla`, `tdmpc`, `vla_jepa`, `vqbet`, `wall_x`, `xvla`): the `Config` dataclass gets a full `Args:` block (including inherited `PreTrainedConfig` fields), and the `<Family>Policy` class gets its public method surface documented, cross-referencing `PreTrainedPolicy`'s base contract and noting only genuine per-policy deviations. Given the scale, this was split across parallel subagents with strict scope boundaries, followed by a manual verification/fixup pass.
- Fixes several real bugs found along the way: `PreTrainedPolicy.forward` had a literal `_summary_`/`_description_` placeholder docstring that had never been filled in; `DiffusionPolicy.__init__` and `VQBeTPolicy.__init__` documented a `dataset_stats` parameter that no longer exists in their signatures; `XVLAPolicy.from_pretrained`'s docstring described a `"model."` prefix-stripping behavior the code doesn't implement (corrected to the actual vendored-Florence-2 remap/tied-embedding-restore behavior); `XVLAAddDomainIdProcessorStep`'s docstring claimed a default of `3` when the field actually defaults to `0`; a handful of dead `"""Input validation (not exhaustive)."""` string statements sat after the first statement in 5 policies' `__post_init__` (never actually docstrings, just inert expressions) and are removed as they were pure dead code.
- Restructured `pyproject.toml`'s `per-file-ignores` for `policies/`: the previous blanket `"src/lerobot/policies/**" = ["D"]` is replaced with per-family enumeration of what's still out of scope (internal building-block files/subdirectories, `modeling_*.py`/`processor_*.py` file patterns whose internals are deferred, `pi_gemma.py`, the new `policies/common/` shared utilities). `configuration_*.py` files are fully checked since they're fully documented.

- Ratchets `interrogate`'s repo-wide `fail-under` from 55 to 58 (measured 59.0% with this PR).

relevant_prs.title: fix(processor): stop silently skipping normalization for multi-dataset checkpoints
relevant_prs.body:
## Summary / Motivation

After the Pipeline migration, normalization and unnormalization are silently skipped at inference for models trained on several datasets. `lerobot/smolvla_base` stores its statistics under `so100.buffer.action`, while `_normalize_action` looks them up under `action`. The lookup misses, `_apply_transform` returns the tensor untouched, and the policy runs on values that are on the wrong scale — with no error and no warning.

The root cause is in the migration script, and the reason it went unnoticed is in the processor. This PR fixes both, and makes the failure mode visible rather than silent.

The trade-off worth flagging: two paths that used to "succeed" now raise. That is deliberate. Both of them were producing or consuming statistics that cannot be correct, and continuing quietly is what let this reach a published checkpoint.

## Related issues

- Related: #4415

## Root cause

Legacy checkpoints trained on several datasets register one buffer per dataset, named `<dataset>_buffer_<feature>` rather than `buffer_<feature>`. Confirmed against the pre-migration revision of `lerobot/smolvla_base` (`3326b100`, the commit before *Convert smolvla with Pipeline (#11)*):

```
normalize_inputs.so100-blue_buffer_observation_state.mean
normalize_targets.so100_buffer_action.mean
unnormalize_outputs.so100-red_buffer_action.mean
```

Running those keys through the old pattern list in `extract_normalization_stats`:

| Key | Matched pattern | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `normalize_inputs.so100_buffer_observation_state.mean` | none | silently discarded |
| `normalize_targets.so100_buffer_action.mean` | `normalize_targets.` | `so100.buffer.action` |
| `unnormalize_outputs.so100_buffer_action.mean` | `unnormalize_outputs.` | `so100.buffer.action` |

Two independent defects combined:

1. `normalize_inputs.buffer_` requires `buffer_` immediately after the module name, so it does not match a dataset-scoped buffer — and the plain `normalize_inputs.` prefix was misspelled `normalalize_inputs.`, so it could never match anything. With both input patterns dead, **every observation statistic was dropped**, while the action statistics survived through the correctly spelled `unnormalize_outputs.` and `normalize_targets.` patterns.
2. `.replace("_", ".")` was applied to the whole buffer name, turning `so100_buffer_action` into the feature name `so100.buffer.action`.

This accounts for all three observed symptoms: the prefix shape, the action statistics surviving, and the observation statistics being absent. The migrated files on the Hub contain exactly six tensors — `{so100, so100-red, so100-blue} × action × {mean, std}` — and nothing else.

## What changed

**`normalize_processor.py`** — make the miss visible and resolvable

- `_required_stats_keys()` lists the keys a step actually looks up at runtime: identity-mapped features and those excluded by `normalize_observation_keys` are skipped, and actions are folded onto the canonical `ACTION` key regardless of the name they carry in `features`.
- `_resolve_prefixed_stats_keys()` runs during `load_state_dict` and remaps a dataset-prefixed key onto the feature name it ends with **when it is the only candidate**. When several datasets provide statistics for the same feature it raises, listing the candidates, instead of picking one arbitrarily — suffix matching alone would have turned a silent skip into a silent application of another dataset's statistics, which is harder to notice, not easier.
- `_warn_on_missing_stats()` reports, once at load time, any feature that will be passed through unchanged for lack of statistics.
- `_apply_transform` splits `norm_mode == IDENTITY or key not in self._tensor_stats` into two branches. Behaviour is unchanged (the hot path stays quiet so inference does not flood the logs), but a deliberate pass-through is now distinguishable in the source from one caused by missing statistics.

**`migrate_policy_normalization.py`** — fix the artifacts at the source

- New `split_dataset_prefix()` separates `<dataset>_buffer_<feature>` into its two parts before the feature name is derived, so the dataset name no longer leaks into it. Single-dataset checkpoints (`buffer_<feature>`) are unaffected.
- Fixed the `normalalize_inputs.` typo, so observation statistics are no longer discarded.
- `extract_normalization_stats` now raises when the state dict holds statistics for more than one dataset. A pipeline stores one set of statistics per feature, so the previous behaviour was "whichever dataset is read last wins".
- Incidental fix: checkpoints using `normalize.buffer_<feature>` previously migrated to the feature name `buffer.action`; they now migrate to `action`.

### Breaking changes

- Loading a multi-dataset checkpoint without supplying statistics now raises instead of returning a silently mis-normalized policy. The message points at `overrides={"normalizer_processor": {"stats": dataset.meta.stats}}`. The standard fine-tuning path is unaffected: it passes `dataset_stats`, which takes the override branch of `load_state_dict` and never reaches this code.
- Migrating a multi-dataset checkpoint now raises. Migrate once per dataset, or attach the statistics at load time.

## How was this tested (or how to run locally)

```
uv run pre-commit run --all-files
uv run pytest tests/processor tests/policies -q
```

On macOS arm64 / MPS, Python 3.14, at `959e0a77`, with `--extra test --extra dev --extra dataset`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pre-commit run` (touched files) | all hooks pass (ruff, typos, pyupgrade, gitleaks, bandit, mypy) |
| `pytest tests/processor` | 420 passed, 105 skipped |
| `pytest tests/policies` | 434 passed, 83 skipped |

Two notes for anyone reproducing this: the pre-commit hook environments pin `python3.12`, so `uv python install 3.12` is needed if the working interpreter is newer; and these counts are higher than the ones reported earlier in this PR because installing the `dataset` extra unskips a large block of tests.

Tests added:

- `tests/processor/test_normalize_processor.py` — single prefix resolved (asserting the values are actually transformed, not merely that the key exists), several prefixes rejected, missing statistics warned about, no warning when statistics are complete, identity features needing none.
- `tests/processor/test_migrate_policy_normalization.py` (new file) — prefix splitting for plain, dataset-scoped and marker-less buffers; unrelated keys ignored; the plain `normalize_inputs.` prefix matched; the dataset prefix stripped; several datasets rejected.
- `test_load_state_dict_does_not_resolve_across_unrelated_feature_suffix` (added in `b7ba5fca`, from review) — a feature named `state` must not adopt `observation.state`'s statistics. Written before the fix and confirmed to fail against the previous matching, which resolved it to the wrong key.

The existing regression tests around `load_state_dict` (`test_state_dict_save_load`, `test_stats_override_preservation_in_load_state_dict`, `test_stats_reconstruction_after_load_state_dict`) and the `hotswap_stats` suite pass unchanged, and no warning noise appears in their output.

Rebased against `upstream/main` (`d0af0577`): no conflicts, and none of the commits landed since branching touch the files in this PR.

Not run: the full `pytest tests` suite, which needs hardware and simulator extras this machine does not have.

## Checklist (required before merge)

- [x] Linting/formatting run (`pre-commit run -a`)
- [x] All tests pass locally (`pytest`) — `tests/processor` and `tests/policies`; the full suite needs extras unavailable here
- [x] Documentation updated — docstrings updated; no user-facing docs affected
- [ ] CI is green — the workflows are held at `action_required` pending maintainer approval
- [x] Community Review: I have reviewed another contributor's open PR and linked it here: #4441

## Reviewer notes

- **The main judgement call is raising rather than guessing.** Both new exceptions replace a path that previously "worked". If you would rather these degrade to warnings, the two call sites are `_resolve_prefixed_stats_keys` and the tail of `extract_normalization_stats`.
- **`lerobot/smolvla_base` is not repaired by this PR.** Its observation statistics are gone from the published artifact and cannot be recovered by any key-resolution logic — re-running the fixed migration against `3326b100` is required. That run will now stop on the multi-dataset guard, which is correct: deciding which of `so100` / `so100-red` / `so100-blue` to publish (or whether to publish three variants) is a call for the maintainers, not the script.
- Worth a close look: `_required_stats_keys()`'s handling of `normalize_observation_keys` and of action features named something other than `action`, since that set drives both the resolution and the warning.
- `split_dataset_prefix` splits on the first `_buffer_`. A feature name legitimately containing that substring would be mis-split; I judged this unlikely enough not to warrant a more elaborate scheme, but flagging it.
- **Left deliberately unfixed:** `feature_name = buffer_name.replace("_", ".")` is still unconditional after the prefix is split off, so a feature whose name legitimately contains an underscore is mangled independently of any dataset prefix — `observation.environment_state` (`OBS_ENV_STATE`, used by ACT, TDMPC and gaussian_actor) migrates to `observation.environment.state` and is then never found at runtime. That is a third distinct defect in this function, it hits single-dataset checkpoints too, and resolving it unambiguously needs the policy's declared feature keys threaded into `extract_normalization_stats`. Keeping it out of this PR so the dataset-prefix change stays reviewable on its own. Filed as #4451.

### Known consequence for inference call sites

These build processors from a pretrained path without passing `dataset_stats`, so they raise against the current `lerobot/smolvla_base` artifact once this lands:

- `src/lerobot/scripts/lerobot_eval.py:776`
- `src/lerobot/async_inference/policy_server.py:157`

This is not new breakage — it is #4415's already-broken artifact surfacing instead of silently propagating a wrong normalization. Resolving it properly is either a re-migrated Hub artifact (fixes every caller at once) or an explicit stats-override path at these call sites; both are maintainer calls, so they are flagged rather than patched here. The training path (`lerobot_train.py:502`) and `rollout/context.py:495` pass `dataset_stats` and are unaffected.

`examples/tutorial/smolvla/using_smolvla_example.py` is self-contained, so it is documented inline instead (`959e0a77`). No statistics are hardcoded there on purpose: the right values depend on which of `so100` / `so100-red` / `so100-blue` the reader runs against, and inventing numbers in an example that drives real hardware would be worse than the bug this PR fixes.

Thanks to @waterEand for catching all of the above in review.

relevant_prs.title: feat(rollout): online task switching for language-conditioned policies
relevant_prs.body:
## Summary / Motivation

Adds runtime task switching to `lerobot-rollout` — the language instruction can be updated while the rollout is running without restart or episode boundary. This enables voice-commanded robots: a speech-to-text (STT) process pipes new tasks into the rollout's stdin and the inference stack picks them up immediately.

**Why this matters**: Language-conditioned policies can now be re-tasked mid-episode without stopping. Common use cases: voice commands, operator corrections, or manual task switching via terminal input. The mechanism is general and pluggable — `stdin` today, HTTP or ZMQ in the future.

Design note: Queue-backed policies (`SmolVLA`, `Pi0`, `Diffusion`, etc.) precompute action chunks; stale actions must be flushed safely when the task switches. We use deferred flush: the listener thread sets a flag, and the main control loop applies the flush from within `select_action()` to avoid queue-consumption races.

The documentation lives at `docs/source/online_task_switching.md`.

Flow:


```
External source (terminal / STT pipe / future HTTP)
         │
         │  new task string
         ▼
  ┌──────────────────────┐
  │     PromptBroker     │  ← thread-safe string holder
  │                      │
  │  register_on_change  │  ← callbacks fired on every switch
  └──────────┬───────────┘
             │ broker.get_task()
       ┌─────┴──────┐
       │            │
       ▼            ▼
  SyncEngine    RTCEngine       ← per-inference-call read
       │            │
       └─────┬──────┘
             │
             ▼
     Recording strategies       ← per-frame read
   (sentry / highlight / dagger)
```
## Related issues

- Closes: none (new feature)
- Related: none

## What changed

- `PromptBroker` — thread-safe task holder with callbacks on change. Supports extensible listeners (stdin, HTTP, ZMQ, etc.).
- Inference engines — `SyncInferenceEngine` and `RTCInferenceEngine` read task per call instead of once at startup.
- Recording strategies — resolve task per frame so dataset frames are labeled with the active task at capture time.
- Deferred flush — PreTrainedPolicy.flush_action_queue() and _apply_pending_flush() prevent queue races when tasks switch. All 14 queue-backed policies apply this at the start of select_action().
- Config — new flags: `--online_task_switching`, `--online_task_switching_source` (default "stdin"), --`online_task_switching_flush` (default true).

**Backward compatible**: When disabled (default), all existing code paths unchanged.

## How was this tested (or how to run locally)

Tests added:

- `tests/test_prompt_broker.py` — 11 unit tests (broker mechanics, listener lifecycle)
- `tests/test_rollout.py` — 3 integration tests (broker + SyncInferenceEngine)
- Run: `pytest -q tests/test_prompt_broker.py tests/test_rollout.py -v`

### Manual verification:

1. Interactive terminal:
```
python examples/online_task_switching/smolvla_demo.py \
    --checkpoint /path/to/smolvla \
    --task "pick up the bottle" \
    --device cuda --flush_on_switch
# Then type new tasks in the terminal
```
2. Via stdin pipe (STT simulation):

```
> /tmp/robot_task
python examples/online_task_switching/smolvla_demo.py \
    --checkpoint ... --device cuda < <(tail -f /tmp/robot_task) &
echo "grab the red cup" >> /tmp/robot_task
```

Observe: logs show task switch immediately, queue is flushed, new action from new task on next tick.

3. Mock robot (no GPU):
```
python examples/online_task_switching/demo.py --fps=2
# Type new tasks interactively
```

## Checklist (required before merge)

- [x] Linting/formatting run (`pre-commit run -a`)
- [x] All tests pass locally (`pytest`)
- [x] Documentation updated
- [ ] CI is green
- [ ] Community Review: I have reviewed another contributor's open PR and linked it here: # (insert PR number/link)

## Reviewer notes

Focus areas:

- Thread safety: `PromptBroker` uses a lock; `flush_action_queue() `/ `_apply_pending_flush() `pattern avoids `listener↔main-thread` races.
- Backward compat: When `online_task_switching=false` (default), all code falls back to static task path.
- Queue-backed policies (×14): All now call `_apply_pending_flush()` at the start of select_action(). Verify consistency across `SmolVLA`, `Pi0`, `Pi0Fast`, `Pi05`, `Diffusion`, `TDMPC`, `VQBeT`, `ACT`, `EO1`, `Groot`, `WallX`, `xVLA,` MultiTaskDiT, `MolmoAct2`.
- Extensibility: Adding a new prompt source requires only subclassing `PromptListenerBase` and registering in `context.py `— no changes to engines or strategies.

relevant_prs.title: fix(processor): preserve dataset-prefixed state stats
relevant_prs.body:
## Summary / Motivation

The normalization migration script does not extract legacy dataset-prefixed state statistics such as `normalize_inputs.so100_buffer_observation_state.mean`. As a result, migrated multi-dataset policies can lose their state normalization stats even when those tensors exist in the source checkpoint. This restores extraction of those stats without changing runtime dataset selection behavior.

## Related issues

- Related: #4415

## What changed

- Match the general `normalize_inputs.` prefix after the existing `normalize_inputs.buffer_` pattern, so dataset-scoped keys stop falling through. `normalize_inputs.buffer_` still comes first and the loop breaks on the first match, so a single-dataset checkpoint still migrates to `observation.state` and `action` exactly as before.
- Remove the misspelled `"normalalize_inputs."` pattern. No checkpoint key can start with that spelling, and it is the only occurrence in the repository, so leaving it beside the correctly spelled entry would mean two patterns for one intent, one of which never fires.
- Add regression coverage for `so100` and `so100-blue` dataset-prefixed state statistics, in a new `tests/processor/test_migrate_policy_normalization.py` alongside the unit it exercises. (`test_migration_detection.py` covers `DataProcessorPipeline._is_processor_config`.)

### One behavior change worth stating explicitly

No runtime API or checkpoint format changes. The **migrated artifact does change**, though, for a checkpoint whose config carries no `normalization_mapping`: `detect_features_and_norm_modes` infers the mode from the extracted statistics, so restoring the state stats changes what the migration writes.

Measured against a state dict with `so100`-scoped input and output buffers and an empty config:

```
         stats keys                                          norm_modes STATE
before   ['so100.buffer.action']                             MIN_MAX
after    ['so100.buffer.action',                             MEAN_STD
          'so100.buffer.observation.state']
```

This is a fix rather than a regression — the checkpoint stored `mean`/`std`, so `MEAN_STD` is the mode it was trained under, and the previous `MIN_MAX` was the hardcoded default at `migrate_policy_normalization.py:242-243` winning by absence. It is called out here because it changes the migrated config for every such checkpoint, which the original description did not say.

## How was this tested (or how to run locally)

- `uv run --extra test --no-sync pytest tests/processor/test_migration_detection.py tests/processor/test_migrate_policy_normalization.py tests/processor/test_normalize_processor.py -q` — 82 passed, 1 skipped.
- `ruff check` passed for the changed files.
- `ruff format --check` passed for the changed files.
- `python -m compileall` passed for the changed files.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Checklist (required before merge)

- [x] Linting/formatting run for changed files (`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`)
- [x] Targeted tests pass locally
- [ ] Documentation updated
- [x] CI is green — 6 checks pass; Build Main Docs was skipped
- [x] Community Review: I have reviewed another contributor's open PR and linked it here: #4285

## Reviewer notes

This is intentionally limited to migration-time extraction. It does not resolve runtime selection among multiple dataset-prefixed stats; choosing a dataset-specific stat still requires separate dataset context and should not silently select the first match.

Two consequences of the same config-inference fallback, both verified, neither a blocker:

- A restored `so100.buffer.observation.state` is also registered as a *feature* and written into the saved processor config, even though it names no real feature. It is inert at runtime: `NormalizerProcessorStep._normalize_observation` (`normalize_processor.py:278-281`) iterates `self.features` but only acts on a key present in the observation, and this one never is.
- The statistics land under `so100.buffer.observation.state` while the runtime looks up `observation.state`. So this PR stops the tensors from being discarded, but does not by itself make #4415's reproduction pass. Whether the dataset prefix should be preserved (as here) or stripped at migration time (as in #4446) is a single decision worth settling once, and I am happy to follow whichever the maintainers prefer.

AI assistance was used during development; the change was reviewed and tested by the contributor.

relevant_prs.title: feat(policies): return a typed prediction alongside actions and show it in Rerun / Foxglove
relevant_prs.body: ## Summary / Motivation - Policies are starting to predict more than actions: imagined frames (LingBot-VA), subtasks and bounding boxes (G0.5). This adds one contract to return them, and `--display_data` shows whatever a policy returns. - Batch in, batch out: `select_action` / `predict_action_chunk` take a batch and return either a bare action tensor (unchanged, every existing policy) or a `PolicyOutput` batch, `{"action": ..., "prediction": ...}`. No new method, no new flag on the CLI. - The prediction is batched like the action (one value per env), and `policy_output_to_transition` turns the output into the `EnvTransition` processors already use. - Turning predictions on is the policy's choice, through its own config (e.g. `--policy.return_predicted_video=true`, or G0.5's System 2). - Every prediction is keyed by what it refers to, reusing existing names: observation keys, annotation language styles, and the annotation pipeline's VQA bbox schema. ``` policy.select_action(batch) ├─ Tensor no prediction this step └─ PolicyOutput {"action": a [B, ...], "prediction": p} p: PolicyPrediction, one value per env observation: {"observation.images.top": frames [B,C,H,W]} predicted future observation language: {"subtask": ["pick up the blue cube", ...]} by annotation style boxes: {"observation.images.top": [{"detections": [ by camera, annotation VQA schema {"label": "cube", "bbox": [x1, y1, x2, y2]}]}, ...]} xyxy, [0, 1] │ ▼ policy_output_to_transition -> EnvTransition(action=a, prediction=p) engine (sync / RTC) only the action goes through the postprocessor ▼ send_next_action -> EnvTransition(action=robot_action_dict, prediction=p) ▼ --display_data first env: Rerun prediction.images.top, prediction.subtask, boxes over the camera Foxglove /prediction/..., /prediction annotations ``` ## Related issues - Related: #4445 (G0.5, stacked on this PR, returns its CoT subtask and boxes through this contract) ## What changed **Contract** - `PolicyOutput`, `PolicyPrediction`, `BboxAnswer` and `Detection` are TypedDicts in `lerobot_types`. `PreTrainedPolicy.select_action` / `predict_action_chunk` return `Tensor | PolicyOutput`. A prediction never changes the actions. - `EnvTransition` gets a `prediction: PolicyPrediction | None` key (`TransitionKey.PREDICTION`); `batch_to_transition` / `transition_to_batch` carry it under the `"prediction"` batch key, so it reaches processor steps. - `create_transition(..., prediction=None)`, `policy_output_to_transition` (normalizes both return types) and `transition_to_prediction` in `lerobot.processor`. **Rollout and callers** - Sync engine: returns the transition when the policy predicted something, otherwise the bare action. RTC: a chunk's prediction is handed out with the next action served, and dropped with the chunk when it is discarded (reset or trained-RTC delay overrun). - `send_next_action` returns the step as a transition (robot action dict + prediction); strategies pass it to `_log_telemetry`. - `lerobot_eval`, `control_utils` and `policy_server` normalize the policy output and keep using the action. **Visualization** - `log_visualization_data(..., policy_step=...)` forwards the prediction to the backend, which shows its first env. - Rerun: predicted frames and text get their own panels (the blueprint grows when they first appear), boxes are drawn over their camera, empty `detections` clears them. - Foxglove: `/prediction/images/`, `/prediction/state`, `/prediction/

relevant_prs.title: Fix loss normalization for padded actions in ACT, Diffusion, and MultiTaskDiT
relevant_prs.body:
## What this fixes

When `action_is_pad` masks out padded timesteps, the subsequent `.mean()` still divides by the total element count (including zeroed-out padding). With 60-70% padding this underestimates the loss by 2-3x, reducing gradient signal and hurting training convergence.

**Before (ACT example):**
```python
l1_loss = (
    F.l1_loss(batch[ACTION], actions_hat, reduction="none")
    * ~batch["action_is_pad"].unsqueeze(-1)
).mean()  # divides by ALL elements including padding
```

**After:**
```python
valid_mask = ~batch["action_is_pad"].unsqueeze(-1)
l1_loss = (
    F.l1_loss(batch[ACTION], actions_hat, reduction="none") * valid_mask
).sum() / valid_mask.sum().clamp_min(1)  # divides by valid elements only
```

## Affected policies

| Policy | File | Fixed |
|--------|------|-------|
| ACT | `modeling_act.py:145` | Yes |
| Diffusion | `modeling_diffusion.py:376` | Yes |
| MultiTaskDiT (DDPM) | `modeling_multi_task_dit.py:689` | Yes |
| MultiTaskDiT (Flow) | `modeling_multi_task_dit.py:753` | Yes |
| TDMPC | `modeling_tdmpc.py` | Not affected (sums over time before batch mean) |

## Test plan

- [ ] `uv run pytest tests/policies -v` passes
- [ ] Verify with a batch where ~50% actions are padded: loss should be higher than before (no dilution)

Fixes #3353

relevant_prs.title: fix(scripts/eval): restore policy training mode after eval_policy()
relevant_prs.body:
## Title

fix(scripts/eval): restore policy training mode after `eval_policy()`

## Summary / Motivation

`eval_policy` in `src/lerobot/scripts/lerobot_eval.py` puts the policy into eval mode before the rollout but never restores the prior mode on return. When called from the training loop (`lerobot_train.py`'s `eval_policy_all → run_one → eval_one → eval_policy` chain), the policy is left in eval mode for every subsequent training step — silently disabling Dropout (no regularisation) and freezing BatchNorm running stats (no further EMA updates). Under DDP only `is_main_process` runs eval (`lerobot_train.py:527`), so the main rank ends up in eval mode while workers stay in train mode, and the all-reduced gradients then combine forward passes computed with different dropout masks and different BN behaviour — a real DDP-correctness issue, not just a regularisation quirk. The fix snapshots `policy.training` on entry and restores it on return; it's a no-op for callers that pass an already-eval-mode policy (e.g. the standalone `lerobot-eval` script).

## Related issues

- Fixes / Closes: #3668 
- Related: # (none)

## What changed

- `src/lerobot/scripts/lerobot_eval.py`: in `eval_policy`, snapshot `policy.training` on entry and restore it before the normal return. Save-and-restore is a strict no-op when the policy is already in eval mode on entry, so the standalone `lerobot-eval` script and any caller that intentionally passes a frozen checkpoint sees no behaviour change.
- Behaviour diff for the training loop: after the first eval, `policy.training` now stays `True` for every subsequent training step (was `False` before). Dropout layers stay active. BatchNorm running stats continue updating. Under DDP, all ranks remain in consistent modes across the all-reduce.
- No breaking changes. No migration steps. Public API of `eval_policy` is unchanged.

**Scope of impact** (which configs / policies were silently degraded):
- Affects every policy with Dropout in its forward path. In-tree: the default **ACT** (6 Dropout layers at p=0.1), Diffusion (vision backbone), VQ-BeT, Multi-Task DiT, X-VLA, plus all VLA policies that inherit Dropout from their pretrained HF backbone (PI0 / PI0.5 / PI0-FAST, SmolVLA, GR00T-N1.5, EO1, Wall-X).
- Triggers from the first eval onward. On the default config (`steps=100k, eval_freq=20k`) that's 80% of training; on the LIBERO / RoboCasa / VLABench example commands in `docs/` (`eval_freq=1k–5k`) it's 95–99% of training.
- Policies using only LayerNorm/GroupNorm and no Dropout (TDMPC, RTC) are unaffected. Policies using `FrozenBatchNorm2d` (ACT's ResNet backbone) are immune to the BN-stat half; the Dropout half still bites.

## How was this tested (or how to run locally)

**Tests added** — `tests/scripts/test_eval.py` (7 tests total, ~1.6s):

```bash
pytest -q tests/scripts/test_eval.py
```

Four regression gates on `eval_policy` itself:
- `test_training_mode_preserved` — policy enters in train mode → leaves in train mode
- `test_eval_mode_preserved` — policy enters in eval mode → leaves in eval mode (protects the standalone `lerobot-eval` flow)
- `test_dropout_remains_active_after_eval_policy` — behavioural check that Dropout still drops on the way out
- `test_eval_policy_does_not_crash_with_canned_rollout[train|eval]` — non-crash for both entry modes

Plus one quantitative mechanism demonstration:
- `test_missing_mode_restoration_hurts_generalisation[0|1]` — trains a tiny Dropout+BatchNorm MLP under the bug pattern vs the fix pattern on identical data and seed, asserts the buggy variant generalises ≥5% worse on a held-out val set. Two seeds for robustness. Runs in ~1.5s. This is what the empirical proof looks like as an executable assertion rather than a separate benchmarks directory.

**Negative case verified.** Reverting the patch makes `test_training_mode_preserved` and `test_dropout_remains_active_after_eval_policy` both fail, confirming the regression gate is doing real work.

**Repeated-run impact numbers** (from local sanity runs of the quantitative test):

| Variant | val_loss | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| BUG (current) | ≈ 0.85–0.90 | trains lower (overfits) but generalises worse |
| FIXED (this PR) | ≈ 0.70–0.75 | 10–25% better val loss on this toy problem |

Real policies (more layers, more Dropout, longer training) generally see larger gaps; the toy MLP is intentionally small so the test stays fast.

## Checklist (required before merge)

- [x] Linting/formatting run (`pre-commit run -a` — passed on all changed files)
- [x] All tests pass locally (`pytest -q tests/scripts/test_eval.py` — 7 passed in ~1.6s)
- [ ] Documentation updated — no doc changes needed (pure bug fix; public API unchanged)
- [ ] CI is green — will be checked once pushed
- [ ] Community Review: I have reviewed another contributor's open PR and linked it here: # (insert PR number/link)

## Reviewer notes

- **Restoration is placed before the normal return only, not in `try`/`finally`.** Exception paths leave the policy in eval mode — same behaviour as before this patch. A `try`/`finally` upgrade would require re-indenting ~165 lines of the existing rollout loop; I kept the patch minimal and reviewable. Happy to land the `try`/`finally` upgrade as a separate cleanup if preferred.
- **Quantitative impact test lives in the test file, not a new directory.** I considered adding a `benchmarks/` folder for the empirical demonstration but folded it into `tests/scripts/test_eval.py` as `test_missing_mode_restoration_hurts_generalisation`. That keeps the proof reproducible from the repo without a new top-level directory, and turns the comparison into an executable assertion that runs in CI.
- **Focus areas for review**: (a) verify the `was_training` save site (just before `policy.eval()`) and the restore site (just before `return info`) are both intended; (b) confirm there's no other caller in the codebase relying on the previous "always returns in eval mode" behaviour — I checked the in-tree callers (`run_one`, the standalone `lerobot-eval` `main()`, the RL `eval_policy.py`) and none of them do.
- Anyone in the community is free to review the PR.

relevant_prs.title: chore(mypy): one ruleset for the whole codebase and mypy 2.3.1
relevant_prs.body:
## Summary / Motivation

- Closing PR of the typing effort (ARCH-07). The 14 PRs below brought every package except `lerobot.rl` under mypy, one module at a time. This PR replaces the 25 per-module overrides with one ruleset, enables the extra checks that were cheap to satisfy everywhere, makes the pre-commit hook check the whole tree, and bumps mypy from 1.19.1 to 2.3.1.
- Excluded: `lerobot.rl` (not typed yet) and the vendored `molmoact2_hf_model`.
- The stricter annotation flags that five modules had on their own are dropped; they should come back repo-wide (see the next candidates in the ruleset).

## Related issues

- Related: ARCH-07 and the per-module PRs listed below.

## What changed

- One `[tool.mypy]` ruleset for all checked code, with a single exception block.
- New checks, each in its own commit with its fixes: `warn_redundant_casts`, `extra_checks`, `strict_bytes` and five error codes (no hits), `strict_equality` (1 fix), `local_partial_types` (1), `truthy-bool` (2), `implicit_reexport = false` (7), `warn_unused_ignores` (36 stale ignores removed) and `ignore-without-code` (1).
- The pre-commit hook now checks the whole tree, so local commits give the same result as CI. Checking only the staged files produced about 43 false errors. Generated `*_pb2` files and gitignored files are skipped.
- mypy 2.3.1 in pre-commit, and the `dev` extra allows `mypy>=2.0.0,<3.0.0`. The two new errors 2.3.1 reports are fixed.
- The next candidates are listed, commented out, in the ruleset: `warn_unreachable`, `strict_equality_for_none`, `check_untyped_defs`.

Breaking changes:

- `lerobot.policies.wall_x.qwen_model` no longer re-exports `Qwen2_5_VLVisionConfig`; import it from `transformers`.
- `LiberoProcessorStep.transform_features` now returns correct features. It was broken, and nothing in the repo calls it.
